Set up the definite integral for the region bounded by the curve, the coordinate axes, and $x = 1$:
$$\text{Integral} = \int_0^1 \frac{1}{2}(x^4 - 1)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\left[ \frac{x^5}{5} - x \right]_0^1$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = 1$ and lower limit $x = 0$:
$$\text{Integral} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{5} - 1\right) - 0 = \frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) = -\frac{2}{5}$$

Take the absolute value for the area of the shaded region below the $x$-axis:
$$\text{Area} = \left| -\frac{2}{5} \right| = \frac{2}{5} \quad (= 0.4)$$

Set up the volume of revolution integral about the $x$-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 1$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^1 y^2\,dx = \pi \int_0^1 \left(\frac{1}{2}(x^4 - 1)\right)^2 dx = \frac{\pi}{4} \int_0^1 (x^8 - 2x^4 + 1)\,dx$$

Express $x^2$ in terms of $y$ from the curve equation $y = \frac{1}{2}(x^4 - 1)$:
$$2y = x^4 - 1 \implies x^4 = 2y + 1 \implies x^2 = (2y + 1)^{\frac{1}{2}}$$

Set up the volume of revolution integral about the $y$-axis from $y = -\frac{1}{2}$ to $y = 0$:
$$V = \pi \int_{-1/2}^0 x^2\,dy = \pi \int_{-1/2}^0 (2y + 1)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dy$$

Integrate using the reverse chain rule:
$$V = \pi \left[ \frac{(2y + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 2} \right]_{-1/2}^0 = \frac{\pi}{3} \left[ (2y + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}} \right]_{-1/2}^0$$

Evaluate at the limits $y = 0$ and $y = -\frac{1}{2}$:
$$V = \frac{\pi}{3}\left((2(0) + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}} - \left(2\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}(1 - 0) = \frac{\pi}{3} \quad (\approx 1.05\text{ cubic units})$$
